headline: Top Five Hold Firm as Week One Delivers Blowouts and Upsets
subhead: The power poll quintet went a combined 5-0 while Tennessee and Arkansas announced themselves with road statement wins.
lead: Week One produced zero movement in the top five of the power poll, but the games themselves were anything but quiet. Two of the five ranked teams won by 18 points or more, while Tennessee and Arkansas flipped scripts on the road to open the season with signature victories.

segments.title: Ohio State Rolls Over Michigan in Rivalry Rout
segments.body: Ohio State led 14-0 after one quarter and 42-7 at the half, never trailing en route to a 42-19 demolition. The Buckeyes forced one turnover and built a 23-point lead, sending an early message that the gap in this rivalry remains wide.

segments.title: Tennessee Stuns Alabama in Knoxville
segments.body: Alabama struck first with a 7-0 lead, but Tennessee erupted for 23 points in the second quarter to cut the halftime deficit to 24-23. The Volunteers forced two turnovers and pushed the margin to 18 by the third quarter en route to a 35-20 statement win.

segments.title: Arkansas Rallies Past Boston College on the Road
segments.body: Boston College led by 8 points at halftime before Arkansas flipped the script. The Razorbacks outscored the Eagles 19-6 over the final two quarters, seizing a 29-20 win with the game's only lead change coming in the second half.

segments.title: Washington and Penn State Smother Season Openers
segments.body: Both top-five teams never trailed. Washington forced two Michigan State turnovers and led by 18 at its peak in a 25-18 win. Penn State forced two Arizona State turnovers, led by 18, and cruised 34-16 to keep the defensive tone set for the conference frontrunners.

segments.title: LSU Outlasts Miami in Bayou Track Meet
segments.body: Three lead changes and a tied first quarter gave way to a 38-27 LSU victory. The Tigers grabbed an 11-point fourth-quarter lead and forced three total turnovers to survive a 65-point affair that felt like a playoff preview in September.

closer: Week Two will test whether Tennessee and Arkansas can sustain their momentum and if the top five can keep the separation intact.
